metadata.case_name: LEUNG KAM MING v. LEE TING LAM

injuries.description: Lower anterior abdominal wall rupture with exposed loops of bowel and urinary bladder
source: his lower anterior abdominal wall was ruptured and loops of bowel and urinary bladder were exposed.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of intra-abdominal organ with pelvic organ

injuries.description: Crush injury of the right hip and thigh
source: his right hip and thigh were crushed,
injuries.icd_description: Crushing injury of hip with thigh

injuries.description: Fracture of the acetabulum and the head of the right femur
injuries.body_part: acetabulum and head of right femur
source: his acetabulum and the head of his right femur were fractured,
injuries.icd_description: Multiple injuries of hip or thigh

injuries.description: Amputation of the right leg by disarticulation of the hip joint (whole femur removed leaving only the socket in the pelvis)
source: His right leg had to be amputated by disarticulation of the hip joint; in other words the whole of the femur was removed leaving only the socket of the hip joint in the pelvis.
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation at right hip joint

source: I find that the Plaintiff lost his right testicle in the accident.
injuries.icd_description: Injury to male genital organ without specification of injury type

injuries.description: Extensive scarring of abdomen and right leg with associated skin loss
source: Notwithstanding these operations he is left with dreadful scars.
This scarring, apart from being so cosmetically disfiguring, has caused problems with the prosthesis, since ulceration has occurred on the right side due to poor fitting and lack of padding.

manifestations.description: phantom limb symptoms, in the form of irritation, itching and formication (that is a feeling of insects on the skin) though these symptoms have now mainly subsided.
Notwithstanding these operations he is left with dreadful scars.
ulceration has occurred on the right side due to poor fitting and lack of padding.

He has to wear a prosthesis, which is secured round his trunk by strapping webbing and buckles. He can move this artificial leg only by tilting the pelvis upwards and swinging the pelvis forwards. He is at present using two crutches. Even if he graduates to using sticks his mobility is bound seriously to be impaired.

He may well have sexual problems. Dr. Wedderburn testified, and I accept his evidence, that the appearance of his abdomen and leg would repel a normal woman. Clearly his chances of getting married and producing a family are gravely impaired. There is a serious risk that, even if he finds someone who is willing to have sexual relations with him, his ability properly to indulge in such relations will be impaired and less satisfactory than would be the case were he possessed of all his physical faculties and unscarred.

He is likely, because of the abnormality of his posture, to develop spondylitis in his spine. This will not seriously affect him, but by the time he reaches the age of 40 - 45 years, he might have to take an odd day off work.

treatments_future: periodic renewal of prosthesis (will require a new prosthesis probably every year or 18 months until age 19; thereafter probably every 3-4 years)

losses.description: Extensive and repellent scarring of the abdomen and leg; possible limited improvement (20-30%) from further plastic surgery; scarring has caused problems with the prosthesis and ulceration.
Mobility is seriously impaired; uses two crutches and can only move prosthesis by tilting and swinging pelvis; even if he graduates to sticks mobility will be seriously impaired.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Clearly he can never indulge in any active pursuits again (e.g. playing football).

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: There is a serious risk that his ability properly to indulge in sexual relations will be impaired and less satisfactory than would be the case were he possessed of all his physical faculties and unscarred.
The appearance of his abdomen and leg would repel a normal woman; his chances of getting married and producing a family are gravely impaired.

Serious loss of future earning capacity; unable to undertake work involving standing, walking or lifting and effectively unable to carry out manual work; competition for white collar work and employers' reluctance to employ physically handicapped persons reduces prospects.
